pieces.file: George Nakashima — rich — the crack is kept.svg
pieces.title: The crack is kept
pieces.caption: When a board split, Nakashima “didn't hide the crack”: he cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it and left it visible, “proof of the repair, not a cover for it”. And the page says who “decided which split earned a butterfly joint and exactly where it sat”. *What is real and what is a choice:* A drawing, not one of his tables. The slab, both splits, the places of the keys and the choice to leave the small split bare are mine. The dark keys stand for a contrasting wood. Setting a key's grain across the board's follows common woodworking practice, not a source about his shop.
pieces.near: He cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it

verdicts.file: George Nakashima — rich — the crack is kept.svg
verdicts.why: Two faults. (1) It is placed beside the wrong paragraph: the anchor "butterfly joint" first matches the Minidoka paragraph, so a pretty slab sits next to "the United States imprisoned him". Anchor it in "The butterfly joint", at "He cut a bowtie-shaped inlay across it". (2) The wood is drawn wrong: the grain runs left to right and the crack runs top to bottom, straight across the grain, with the keys lying along the grain.

remade.file: George Nakashima — rich — the crack is kept.svg
remade.what: The crack ran across the grain from edge to edge with red keys lying along it, and the piece sat beside the Minidoka paragraph. The split now runs with the grain in from one end, two dark keys stand across it, a second small split is left without a key for the page's point that he chose, the Dovetail avatar is dropped, and the anchor moves to the butterfly-joint section.
remade.by: a dispatched workshop maker, a child, from the challenger's report; looked over by the working session; placed by the Concierge
remade.second_verdict: none: the remake has not been challenged again
